hot.title: Hyperagents
hot.summary: Researchers at multiple institutions including the University of British Columbia and Meta developed HyperAgents, a framework enabling AI systems to autonomously modify their own self-improvement mechanisms, extending recursive self-improvement beyond coding tasks. This approach achieved 0.710 accuracy in paper review and 0.372 performance in robotics reward design, while also demonstrating transferable meta-level improvements to new domains.

hot.title: End-to-End Training for Unified Tokenization and Latent Denoising
hot.summary: UNITE introduces a single-stage, end-to-end training framework that unifies image tokenization and latent diffusion denoising within a single, shared-parameter Generative Encoder. This method achieves competitive generative performance with an FID of 1.73 for UNITE-L on ImageNet 256x256 and strong reconstruction fidelity without relying on multi-stage training or external pretrained visual encoders.

hot.title: Memento-Skills: Let Agents Design Agents
hot.summary: Memento-Skills introduces a system for Large Language Model (LLM) agents to continually learn and improve without updating core model parameters, treating reusable skills as an external, evolving memory. The system achieved a 13.7 percentage-point increase in test accuracy on the GAIA benchmark and more than doubled the baseline performance on the HLE dataset, enabling autonomous agent design and adaptation.

hot.title: AVO: Agentic Variation Operators for Autonomous Evolutionary Search
hot.summary: Agentic Variation Operators (AVO) empower large language models to function as autonomous, iterative optimizers in evolutionary search for high-performance code. This framework successfully discovered multi-head attention kernels on NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs that achieved up to 3.5% higher throughput than cuDNN and 10.5% higher than FlashAttention-4, alongside effective transferability to grouped-query attention.

hot.title: GameplayQA: A Benchmarking Framework for Decision-Dense POV-Synced Multi-Video Understanding of 3D Virtual Agents
hot.summary: Researchers at the University of Southern California introduce GAMEPLAYQA, a benchmarking framework designed to evaluate Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on agentic perception and reasoning within decision-dense, multi-video 3D virtual environments. The framework reveals that current MLLMs exhibit substantial performance gaps compared to human capabilities, especially in tasks requiring precise temporal tracking and cross-viewpoint synchronization.

hot.title: CanViT: Toward Active-Vision Foundation Models
hot.summary: CanViT introduces the first task- and policy-agnostic Active-Vision Foundation Model, integrating a recurrent Vision Transformer with a scene-wide memory to process visual scenes from sequences of localized glimpses. The model achieved 38.5% mIoU on ADE20K semantic segmentation from a single glimpse, outperforming previous active vision models while using 19.5x fewer FLOPs, and demonstrated strong generalization across various policies and resolutions.

hot.title: Do World Action Models Generalize Better than VLAs? A Robustness Study
hot.summary: Researchers from Huawei Technologies and the University of Toronto systematically compared World Action Models (WAMs) and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies under various environmental and linguistic perturbations. The study found WAMs generally more robust to visual perturbations, benefiting from spatiotemporal priors from video pretraining, but significantly slower in inference speed compared to VLAs.

hot.title: Speed by Simplicity: A Single-Stream Architecture for Fast Audio-Video Generative Foundation Model
hot.summary: daVinci-MagiHuman, an open-source audio-video generative foundation model, leverages a single-stream Transformer architecture to jointly produce synchronized human-centric video and audio. It demonstrates competitive generation quality and efficiency, outperforming open-source baselines in visual quality, text alignment, and speech intelligibility, while enabling fast inference.

hot.title: Repurposing Geometric Foundation Models for Multi-view Diffusion
hot.summary: Researchers from KAIST AI introduce Geometric Latent Diffusion (GLD), a framework that repurposes the multi-level feature space of geometric foundation models as the latent space for multi-view diffusion. This approach yields enhanced geometric consistency and photorealistic quality in Novel View Synthesis (NVS) while demonstrating 4.4x faster training convergence and robust zero-shot 3D geometry decoding.

hot.title: Foundations of Schrödinger Bridges for Generative Modeling
hot.summary:
Sophia Tang's work establishes Schr
Rodinger bridges (SB) as a unifying mathematical framework for modern generative models, including diffusion and flow matching, across both continuous and discrete state spaces. The paper provides a comprehensive theoretical guide detailing the underlying principles, dynamic formulations, and practical construction methods for these advanced stochastic processes.

hot.title: WildWorld: A Large-Scale Dataset for Dynamic World Modeling with Actions and Explicit State toward Generative ARPG
hot.summary: Researchers from Alaya Studio, Beijing Institute of Technology, and Tsinghua University introduced WildWorld, a large-scale dataset of over 108 million frames from the AAA game *Monster Hunter: Wilds*, offering explicit state and action annotations to enhance the learning of dynamic world models. The accompanying WildBench benchmark, featuring novel Action Following and State Alignment metrics, effectively evaluates models' ability to adhere to actions and maintain state consistency, with state-aware models demonstrating improved interaction fidelity and long-horizon prediction.

hot.title: UniGRPO: Unified Policy Optimization for Reasoning-Driven Visual Generation
hot.summary: A unified Reinforcement Learning framework, UniGRPO, jointly optimizes discrete language and continuous visual policies for interleaved multimodal generation, achieving superior performance on text alignment and compositional benchmarks. The framework integrates GRPO for text and FlowGRPO for images, while introducing key modifications for scalability and stability.

hot.title: On the Direction of RLVR Updates for LLM Reasoning: Identification and Exploitation
hot.summary: Researchers at Alibaba Group identified that the direction of policy updates, quantified by signed log probability difference (∆ log p), is more informative than update magnitude for understanding RLVR's impact on LLM reasoning. This directional analysis reveals RLVR's sparse updates concentrate on low-probability, reasoning-critical tokens, leading to a test-time extrapolation method that boosted Avg@32 scores by up to 2.92 points and a training-time reweighting method that increased Avg@32 by an average of 1.63 points on math benchmarks.

hot.title: ThinkJEPA: Empowering Latent World Models with Large Vision-Language Reasoning Model
hot.summary: ThinkJEPA integrates a Vision-Language Model to semantically guide a JEPA-style latent world model, improving representation quality and achieving up to 14% lower Average Displacement Error (ADE) and 15% lower Final Displacement Error (FDE) in hand-manipulation trajectory prediction compared to V-JEPA baselines.

hot.title: PivotRL: High Accuracy Agentic Post-Training at Low Compute Cost
hot.summary: PivotRL is a post-training framework for Large Language Models that combines the computational efficiency of Supervised Fine-Tuning with the generalization capabilities of End-to-End Reinforcement Learning for long-horizon agentic tasks. It achieved an average of +14.11 percentage points in-domain accuracy improvement and robustly retained out-of-domain performance, requiring significantly less compute than End-to-End RL.

hot.title: MCLR: Improving Conditional Modeling in Visual Generative Models via Inter-Class Likelihood-Ratio Maximization and Establishing the Equivalence between Classifier-Free Guidance and Alignment Objectives
hot.summary: Researchers from the University of Michigan and Michigan State University introduced MCLR (Maximum Inter-Class Likelihood-Ratio Training), a principled objective that improves conditional modeling in visual generative models, enabling high-quality conditional generation without classifier-free guidance (CFG). The work also formally establishes CFG as an implicit inference-time alignment algorithm that minimizes a weighted inter-class likelihood-ratio objective.

hot.title: MinerU-Diffusion: Rethinking Document OCR as Inverse Rendering via Diffusion Decoding
hot.summary: MinerU-Diffusion re-frames document OCR as an inverse rendering problem, employing a diffusion decoder to achieve up to 3.2 times faster inference with enhanced robustness against semantic distortions compared to autoregressive methods, while maintaining competitive accuracy on full-document parsing benchmarks.

hot.title: ABot-PhysWorld: Interactive World Foundation Model for Robotic Manipulation with Physics Alignment
hot.summary: ABot-PhysWorld, developed by AMAP CV Lab, Alibaba Group, is an interactive world foundation model for robotic manipulation that generates visually realistic and physically plausible videos with action control. It achieved the highest reported average score of 0.8491 on PBench, showing superior physical plausibility (0.9306 Domain Score) while maintaining competitive visual quality, and established state-of-the-art zero-shot generalization on EZSbench with an overall average score of 0.8030.

hot.title: Omni-WorldBench: Towards a Comprehensive Interaction-Centric Evaluation for World Models
hot.summary: Omni-WorldBench introduces a new benchmark and evaluation protocol to assess the interactive response capabilities of video-based world models in 4D settings. The study evaluates 18 models, revealing their strengths in visual fidelity but identifying limitations in causal consistency and robust joint control over camera and objects.

hot.title: Off-Policy Value-Based Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models
hot.summary: ReVal introduces an off-policy value-based reinforcement learning framework for large language models that interprets LLM logits as Q-values and utilizes a replay buffer for efficient experience reuse. This approach achieved an average of 4.3x speedup in convergence and an 18% reduction in wall-clock training time on mathematical reasoning tasks while outperforming on-policy baselines.

likes.title: Perception Encoder: The best visual embeddings are not at the output of  the network
likes.summary: Perception Encoder introduces a family of vision models that achieve state-of-the-art performance across diverse vision and vision-language tasks, demonstrating that general, high-quality visual features can be extracted from the intermediate layers of a single, contrastively-trained network. It provides specific alignment tuning methods to make these features accessible for tasks ranging from zero-shot classification to dense spatial prediction and multimodal language understanding.

likes.title: TTRL: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: TTRL is a framework enabling Large Language Models to self-improve through Reinforcement Learning on unlabeled test data, using self-generated rewards derived from majority voting. This approach substantially boosts performance on complex reasoning tasks, with one model achieving a 211% improvement on AIME 2024, by fostering a self-reinforcing learning loop.

likes.title: Inference-Time Scaling for Generalist Reward Modeling
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI and Tsinghua University developed Self-Principled Critique Tuning (SPCT) and DeepSeek-GRM models, a pointwise generative reward modeling approach that achieves state-of-the-art performance in generalist reward benchmarks. This method demonstrates effective inference-time scalability, allowing smaller models to match or exceed the performance of much larger models by leveraging increased compute during inference, thereby improving LLM alignment.

likes.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
likes.summary: Research from Tsinghua University reveals that current Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) primarily enhances the sampling efficiency of Large Language Models for already existing reasoning patterns. This optimization often narrows the models' overall reasoning capacity at higher pass@k values, contrasting with distillation, which effectively expands their problem-solving scope.

likes.title: Reasoning Models Can Be Effective Without Thinking
likes.summary: Ma et al. demonstrated that Large Language Models trained for Chain-of-Thought reasoning can achieve comparable or superior performance without generating explicit reasoning steps, utilizing a technique called 'NoThinking'. This approach significantly reduces inference latency by up to 9x and token usage by up to 5.1x, particularly when combined with parallel sampling, offering a more efficient paradigm for LLM reasoning.

likes.title: Synthetic Data Generation & Multi-Step RL for Reasoning & Tool Use
likes.summary: SWiRL is an offline multi-step reinforcement learning methodology designed to enhance Large Language Models' reasoning and tool-use capabilities. It generates and utilizes synthetic data, applying process-based filtering for step-wise optimization, which leads to substantial performance gains and strong cross-domain generalization in complex tasks.

likes.title: ReTool: Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Tool Use in LLMs
likes.summary: ReTool, developed by ByteDance Seed, introduces a reinforcement learning framework that enables Large Language Models to strategically use code interpreters for complex problem-solving. It achieved 67.0% accuracy on the AIME 2024 benchmark, significantly improving performance over text-based reasoning and demonstrating emergent self-correction capabilities in code generation.

likes.title: Hogwild! Inference: Parallel LLM Generation via Concurrent Attention
likes.summary: Researchers from Yandex, HSE University, and IST Austria developed "Hogwild! Inference," a protocol enabling multiple Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate text concurrently by sharing a dynamically updated attention Key-Value (KV) cache. This mechanism allows LLMs to self-organize and collaborate in real-time, achieving up to 3.6x speedup and improved accuracy on complex reasoning tasks.

likes.title: Challenges and Paths Towards AI for Software Engineering
likes.summary: This paper presents a strategic roadmap for the field of AI in software engineering, providing a comprehensive taxonomy of software development tasks and identifying nine key bottlenecks that impede current AI capabilities. It proposes a targeted set of research directions focused on data collection, training, and inference-time approaches to advance automated software development.

likes.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
likes.summary: Researchers from ByteDance Seed, Tsinghua University, and The University of Hong Kong developed DAPO, an open-source reinforcement learning system for large language models. The system achieved 50 points on the AIME 2024 dataset with a Qwen2.5-32B model, surpassing the prior 47-point score of DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B while requiring 50% fewer training steps.

likes.title: Proof or Bluff? Evaluating LLMs on 2025 USA Math Olympiad
likes.summary: Researchers from ETH Zurich and INSAIT conducted the first evaluation of large language models on generating rigorous natural language proofs for problems from the 2025 USA Mathematical Olympiad. The study found that most state-of-the-art models scored below 5% of the maximum points, with the highest-performing model, GEMINI-2.5-PRO, achieving only 24.4%, demonstrating fundamental shortcomings in advanced mathematical reasoning capabilities.

likes.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI developed DeepSeek-R1, an LLM demonstrating that sophisticated reasoning capabilities can emerge through pure outcome-based reinforcement learning without reliance on human-annotated reasoning trajectories. The model achieved an AIME 2024 pass@1 accuracy of 77.9% with R1-Zero, and the multi-stage DeepSeek-R1 surpassed state-of-the-art models on numerous math, coding, and STEM benchmarks while exhibiting emergent self-reflection and dynamic strategy adaptation.

likes.title: ReSearch: Learning to Reason with Search for LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: The ReSearch framework enables Large Language Models to integrate multi-step reasoning with external search, learning interactively via reinforcement learning without supervised intermediate steps. It yields substantial performance gains on complex multi-hop question answering benchmarks and reveals emergent self-correction capabilities.

likes.title: Insights into DeepSeek-V3: Scaling Challenges and Reflections on Hardware for AI Architectures
likes.summary: DeepSeek-V3 showcases how a hardware-software co-design strategy can achieve state-of-the-art large language model performance using a comparatively modest cluster of 2,048 NVIDIA H800 GPUs. The paper highlights innovations like Multi-head Latent Attention, DeepSeekMoE, FP8 mixed-precision training, and a Multi-Plane Fat-Tree network, which collectively reduce memory consumption, lower training costs, and accelerate inference.

likes.title: One-Minute Video Generation with Test-Time Training
likes.summary: Researchers from NVIDIA and leading universities introduce Test-Time Training (TTT) layers within pre-trained Diffusion Transformers to generate one-minute-long videos from text storyboards, enabling coherent multi-scene narratives while addressing the computational limitations of traditional self-attention mechanisms for long sequences.

likes.title: Sequential Task Assignment and Resource Allocation in V2X-Enabled Mobile  Edge Computing
likes.summary: A multi-tier task offloading mechanism for V2X-enabled Mobile Edge Computing efficiently processes sequential subtasks from vehicular applications by first leveraging proximate vehicle resources and then RSU-based MEC. The system minimizes energy consumption while meeting stringent delay requirements through joint optimization of offloading decisions, communication, and computation resource allocation, demonstrating superior performance over various baselines.

likes.title: How new data permeates LLM knowledge and how to dilute it
likes.summary: Research from Google DeepMind reveals how new knowledge permeates through large language models, demonstrating that surprising information (measured by token probability) leads to broader changes across model behavior, while introducing "stepping-stone" text augmentation and "ignore-k" update pruning techniques that reduce undesirable priming effects by 50-95%.

likes.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
likes.summary: Titans introduces a new neural memory module that learns to memorize information at test time and effectively combines with attention mechanisms for better long-term sequence modeling

likes.title: PHYBench: Holistic Evaluation of Physical Perception and Reasoning in  Large Language Models
likes.summary: PHYBench, a new benchmark developed by the School of Physics at Peking University, rigorously evaluates large language models' physical perception and reasoning using 500 original, human-curated physics problems. Evaluations revealed a substantial performance gap between LLMs and human experts, with the best LLM achieving 36.9% accuracy compared to the human baseline of 61.9%.

likes.title: Transformers without Normalization
likes.summary: This research introduces Dynamic Tanh (DyT), a simple element-wise function designed as a drop-in replacement for normalization layers in Transformers. Models equipped with DyT achieve performance comparable to or exceeding their normalized counterparts across a wide range of tasks including computer vision, large language models, and speech processing, often without requiring extensive hyperparameter tuning.
